notes: Extracted 29 October 2026 from the guide (src/guides/segmentedtrack.guide.tsx) and docs/evidence/segmentedtrack.md at 889444e (“docs: publish the #194–#211 Coin fixes to their guides”, 13 October). The guide's Sources note was checked on 13 October 2026 on the build it calls the 12 October build (mirror v0.1.78-c1fa197, Biscuit's main at c1fa197, the evidence's c1fa197 publish section), so items citing it carry 2026-10-13 and 0.1.78-c1fa197. The evidence has sections from 5 October (3795b4c), 8 October (636f3f5) and 13 October (c1fa197); later sections replace earlier ones, and each item citing the evidence carries its section's date and build. Installed build: jfs-components 0.1.78, mirror v0.1.78-dbe0e02 (Biscuit's main at dbe0e02, 27 October). GitHub's compare of v0.1.78-c1fa197 and v0.1.78-dbe0e02 (293 files, complete) touches no SegmentedTrack, MetricLegendItem, RangeTrack, resolver or token file. Installed SegmentedTrack.tsx matches every guide and evidence sentence used here, read from source, not run (token values through the package's own getVariableByName): the track merges Appearance / DataViz Senary under the provider's and its own modes (lines 180–185); its height is segmentedTrack/height, 24, with radius half of it (187–189); the root is a row, width 100%, overflow hidden, transparent, with no gap (206–215); a slice is flex: value with minWidth 1, so 0 keeps a 1 px sliver and a missing value counts as 1 (139–147, 272); segments={[]} renders no slices and leaving segments out renders three equal default slices (105–109, 262); each slice gets Emphasis / DataViz High, Medium, Low by index, repeating, over the track's modes and under the segment's own (103–118, 264–268); on the web the root is role group with aria-label from accessibilityLabel and accessible false (199–205), and a slice with its own accessibilityLabel is an accessible image (131–138); nothing is pressable, and react-native-web 0.21.2 gives a role-img element no tabIndex, so it can't take focus. Light dataViz/bg values: Senary 206,161,90 / 232,188,122 / 253,232,201 (strong to light); Primary 93,0,181 / 201,183,255 / 237,231,255 (purple); Neutral 204,207,209 / 224,224,227 / 245,245,245. Contradicted by the installed build and left out: the Do & Don't pair “Use a data appearance / Pick Neutral”, whose reason “All three slices turn the same grey and the split disappears.” no longer holds: the token file at 3795b4c mapped Neutral's high, medium and low dataViz bg all to mode/Grey/2400 (the evidence's “Neutral: rgb(245,245,245) for all three”), but since 636f3f5, unchanged on dbe0e02, they map to Grey/2000, 2200 and 2400, three distinct greys. #197 (Components, To do) records the old behaviour; its Do caption “Senary gives three distinct golds.” is kept as a configuration rule. Not contradicted but wrong on the page: the Configuration “Primary appearance” specimen and the playground's Primary option pass only Color Mode Light, so since the Senary default (636f3f5) they render gold, not the purple their caption describes; the caption is kept for Appearance / DataViz Primary, which the resolver confirms is purple. Out of date and not used: the Sources “Installed jfs-components is 0.1.78 (12 October build)”, and the 5 October evidence lines superseded by later sections (purple default, role img, empty list painting three slices, no testID, Neutral 245 for all three). Not recorded: style, segmentStyle, children with SegmentedTrack.Segment, a segment's color and modes, testID, which the guide doesn't cover (and the building rules keep colour overrides off Coin components); the evidence's Figma node details and Biscuit's unpublished SegmentedTrack.mdx pointers (SegmentedControl, CoverageBarComparison, LinearProgress), which the guide doesn't say, so the progress-bar avoidWhen names no component; dark mode (#197's reversed emphasis: Dark Senary 143,99,23 / 99,69,20 / 36,26,10), which the pack's rules keep out of gaps. Anatomy: only the Track is always present; slices come from the data (an empty list has none). content.bad is empty: “KYC 70% complete” is the Don't's label for a misuse, not bad copy. Gap: the Sources note's stale Storybook (in #196's list); on 29 October the published index.json (last modified 17 October 2026) still lists only the pre-0.1.78 SegmentedTrack stories (all-appearances, custom-colors, slot-children and the others), none of upstream's segments, emphasis or empty. Examples follow the building rules: no Color Mode, and no modes on SegmentedTrack, Card, VStack or Text (the guide sets Light and Senary on all of them, and Senary is the track's default); the guide's width 100% styles are dropped, since Card's content column and VStack stretch their children (Card.tsx contentWrapperStyle, stackAlignment.ts). MetricLegendItem has no entry in this pack; the examples use it because the guide's legend is MetricLegendItem rows (as is Range Track's own), no component with an entry draws a coloured dot beside a name and share, and the guide says to pair the track with a legend. It is the one place modes are set, following the evidence rule in placementAdvice: Appearance / DataViz Senary and Emphasis / DataViz by position, because MetricLegendItem reads only its own modes (no useTokens, no Senary default) and would otherwise draw Primary purple dots (93,0,181 at High) beside gold slices; Color Mode still reaches it through the VStack, which clones the provider's modes into its children with the child's own modes winning (VStack.tsx 63–64, 89–92). Text has an undocumented entry and takes text. Copy is the guide's own (Portfolio mix, ₹4,20,000 invested, Equity 60%, Debt 25%, Cash 15%, the five-part mix, its spoken names, No investments yet). Left out of examples (three at most): Equal slices, Weighted slices alone, Primary appearance, A zero share, No data's empty track, the Don'ts and the playground. Sorting (batch 8): the cross-check found that the Appearance / DataViz fact added a precedence (provider and own modes over the Senary default) that no evidence line states; it now says only what the evidence does. It also found the Emphasis / DataViz order stated with no condition, where the evidence checked it in Light; it now says so. Refreshed 29 October 2026 for guide fix #543 (3f56271): the Anatomy description now calls the track a 24 px bar with fully rounded ends; /anatomy/0 says so in its own words (its quote is unchanged).

examples.purpose: A portfolio card, the guide's In context: the screen works out each part's share and passes the same list, in the same order, to the track and the legend, so their colours match. The track keeps its default Senary gold and is named by its spoken name; each MetricLegendItem carries Senary and its slice's emphasis (High, Medium, Low), so its dot takes its slice's colour.
examples.jsx:
<Card>
  <VStack>
    <Text text="Portfolio mix" />
    <Text text="₹4,20,000 invested" />
    <SegmentedTrack
      segments={[
        { key: 'Equity', value: 60 },
        { key: 'Debt', value: 25 },
        { key: 'Cash', value: 15 },
      ]}
      accessibilityLabel="Portfolio mix: equity 60%, debt 25%, cash 15%"
    />
    <VStack>
      <MetricLegendItem label="Equity" value="60%" modes={{ 'Appearance / DataViz': 'Senary', 'Emphasis / DataViz': 'High' }} />
      <MetricLegendItem label="Debt" value="25%" modes={{ 'Appearance / DataViz': 'Senary', 'Emphasis / DataViz': 'Medium' }} />
      <MetricLegendItem label="Cash" value="15%" modes={{ 'Appearance / DataViz': 'Senary', 'Emphasis / DataViz': 'Low' }} />
    </VStack>
  </VStack>
</Card>

evidenceFacts.name: Appearance / DataViz
evidenceFacts.description: A track with no modes has Senary gold slices (206,161,90 / 232,188,122 / 253,232,201 at High, Medium, Low), as in Figma, not the collection's default Primary (purple). An appearance recolours every slice.
evidenceFacts.quote: The default slices are Senary gold (206,161,90 / 232,188,122 / 253,232,201).

evidenceFacts.name: Emphasis / DataViz
evidenceFacts.description: Set on each slice by its position: High, Medium, Low, then repeating, as checked in Light (the guide shows Light only). An Emphasis / DataViz on the track itself is overwritten; a segment's own modes win.
evidenceFacts.quote: Slice colour is `dataViz/bg` with `Emphasis / DataViz` cycling High, Medium, Low by index (the track's own Emphasis is overwritten; a segment's `modes` can change it).

evidenceFacts.name: segments
evidenceFacts.description: Each part's value sets its width as a share of the total (flex: value; a missing value counts as 1; 0 keeps a 1 px sliver). An empty list draws an empty, transparent 24 px track; leaving segments out draws three equal default slices.
evidenceFacts.quote: An empty `segments` list renders an empty, transparent 24 px track instead of three default slices (omitting `segments` still gives three equal slices).

evidenceFacts.name: accessibilityLabel
evidenceFacts.description: The track's spoken name. On the web the track is a group (role group) named by it.
evidenceFacts.quote: On the web the track is `role="group"` named by `accessibilityLabel`
